questions.q: Butan-2-one is treated with ethylmagnesium bromide in dry ether, followed by H₃O⁺. The product is:
questions.explain: The ethyl group adds to the carbonyl carbon and work-up protonates the alkoxide, so the ketone gives a tertiary alcohol, (C₂H₅)₂C(OH)CH₃. A secondary alcohol would come from an aldehyde.

questions.q: How many moles of methane are released when one mole of prop-2-yn-1-ol, HC≡C–CH₂OH, is treated with excess CH₃MgBr?
questions.explain: Each acidic hydrogen destroys one CH₃MgBr and releases one CH₄; this molecule has one O–H and one terminal alkyne C–H. The CH₂ hydrogens are not acidic.

questions.q: But-3-en-2-one (CH₂=CH–CO–CH₃) is treated with CH₃MgBr in the presence of CuBr, then H₃O⁺. The main product is:
questions.explain: With copper(I) the reagent becomes a soft organocopper nucleophile and adds 1,4; the enolate formed tautomerises to the saturated ketone. Without CuBr the hard Grignard reagent adds 1,2 to give 2-methylbut-3-en-2-ol.

questions.q: Which halide does NOT form a Grignard reagent with ordinary magnesium in dry ether?
questions.explain: The C–F bond is too strong for ordinary magnesium, so alkyl fluorides are not used. Chlorides, bromides and iodides, including aryl bromides, react.
